scope: Proposition 11.22 (Maximality of an unbalanced ordered splitting) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 97. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let V = W ⊕ U, with 0 < dim U < dim W, be a nondegenerate splitting in an isometry type, or an image–kernel splitting in linear type with anti-actions. Let M be a group of the corresponding classical actions containing the natural special group, and let K be the full ordered splitting stabilizer, equivalently the idempotent stabilizer for the ring action. Assume that K supplements the special group in M, that its collineations act semilinearly irreducibly on U, and that the supported special group on W is available, as is that on U when dim U is large. In the linear case assume also that K contains an anti-action fixing the projector, hence carrying its image–kernel data into the dual annihilator data. For sufficiently large dim W, the subgroup K is maximal in M.
